analysis: The changes are documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (line 52 in the patch; the supplied head excerpts at lines 1308-1821 are unchanged context) and docs/threat-model.yaml (lines 1969-1970). No executable code changed, so no new runtime attack surface is introduced by this PR. The threat-model edit widens the documented provider media-ingestion allowlist for inline videos to data:video/mp4, x-m4v, quicktime and mov. It adds the condition that the payload bytes be an MP4 or QuickTime file. The existing caps are retained: decoded-byte, duration, frame-pixel, video-count and aggregate limits, plus rejection of http(s), file and unsupported MIME types. The AVURLAssetReferenceRestrictions.forbidAll mitigation text is unchanged. This is relevant to T-050 (inline video plaintext in provider temp files), TB-003 and TB-007. I could not verify that the underlying Swift (MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders and the byte-sniffing logic) actually implements the byte-signature check or that the caps apply to the new labels, because that source is not in the supplied units. The documented behavior is more restrictive than a MIME-only check, so the docs do not claim weaker controls. A later source-pass review of the corresponding code change should confirm the signature validation, that no temp-file plaintext regression (T-050) is introduced, and that variable-frame-rate handling does not bypass the duration or frame caps. The cli-reference unit text covers prefix cache, fan control, logout and App Attest passthrough docs. Those statements are consistent with the existing threat model (T-041, TB-010, T-053) and carry no new security claims from this PR.
